title: Multilingual Knowledge Transfer under Data Constraints via Lexical Interventions
gist: Apple researchers propose LINK, a near-zero-cost pretraining method that swaps words in high-resource (English) training data with bilingual-vocabulary translations, and show across eight languages and five model sizes it delivers up to a 2x training speedup to reach equivalent downstream performance in low-resource target languages without any translation systems, auxiliary models, or extra training stages.

insights.claim: When target-language training data is scarce, a multilingual model must acquire most of the knowledge needed for tasks like scientific reasoning, commonsense inference, and world knowledge from the high-resource language, making effective cross-lingual knowledge transfer essential rather than optional.
insights.speaker: Apple ML Research
insights.so_what: Any company building or fine-tuning multilingual models for markets with limited native-language text (many emerging-market languages) faces a structural data ceiling that ordinary scaling can't fix without transfer techniques.
insights.quote: the knowledge required for many downstream tasks involving scientific reasoning, commonsense inference, and world knowledge must be acquired primarily from the high-resource language
insights.locator: Multilingual Knowledge Transfer under Data Constraints via Lexical Interventions abstract

insights.claim: Existing methods for improving cross-lingual knowledge transfer require large amounts of parallel data, translation systems, auxiliary models, or additional training stages, resources that are largely unavailable for most languages, which is the gap LINK is designed to close.
insights.speaker: Apple ML Research
insights.so_what: Prior state-of-the-art transfer techniques are effectively inaccessible to teams working on truly low-resource languages, which is the addressable gap LINK targets and a differentiator versus competing approaches.
insights.quote: Existing methods for improving such cross-lingual knowledge transfer require large amounts of parallel data, translation systems, auxiliary models, or additional training stages that are largely unavailable for many languages
insights.locator: Multilingual Knowledge Transfer under Data Constraints via Lexical Interventions abstract

themes.theme: LINK: lexical substitution as a pretraining intervention

insights.claim: LINK improves knowledge transfer during model pretraining by randomly swapping words in a portion of the high-resource (English) training corpus with their word-level translations from a bilingual vocabulary, requiring no additional model training and no resource beyond a bilingual vocabulary that can be obtained at near-zero cost for virtually any language.
insights.speaker: Apple ML Research
insights.so_what: A near-zero-cost data intervention that needs only a bilingual word list (not parallel corpora or extra models) dramatically lowers the barrier to improving low-resource-language model quality, making it viable even for organizations without large translation infrastructure.
insights.quote: randomly selected words in a portion of the high-resource (English) training corpus are swapped with their word-level translations, requiring no additional model training and only a bilingual vocabulary, which can be obtained at near-zero cost for virtually any language
insights.locator: Multilingual Knowledge Transfer under Data Constraints via Lexical Interventions abstract

insights.claim: Evaluated on eight languages across five model sizes, LINK produces notable downstream-task improvements in the target language, including up to a 2x speedup in training time needed to reach equivalent performance versus baseline approaches.
insights.speaker: Apple ML Research
insights.so_what: A roughly 2x reduction in compute/time-to-parity for low-resource-language pretraining is a material cost lever for any lab training multilingual models, directly cutting GPU-hours per unit of target-language quality.
insights.quote: Evaluation on eight languages across five model sizes shows notable improvements on downstream tasks in the target language, with up to a 2x speedup in training to reach equivalent performance.
insights.locator: Multilingual Knowledge Transfer under Data Constraints via Lexical Interventions abstract
